covenants.name: Leverage Ratio
covenants.quote: The Company will not permit the Leverage Ratio on the last day of any Test Period to exceed 3.25 to 1.00

parsed.notes: Investment-grade style unsecured revolver with ratings-based and sustainability-linked pricing. The only financial maintenance covenant is the Leverage Ratio (Section 6.06), tested at the end of each fiscal quarter on a trailing four-quarter basis. It is a net ratio: Consolidated Total Indebtedness is reduced by the lesser of US-held cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and $2.5bn. Acquisition Indebtedness for a signed but unconsummated Material Acquisition is disregarded. Acquisition holiday: if an Acquisition (or series within 180 days) involves $1bn or more of incurred or assumed debt and raises pro forma leverage, the Company may elect within 30 days to raise the maximum to 3.75x. The higher level applies for the quarter of closing and the next three quarters, and the Company can end it early by notice. A new election requires at least two consecutive quarters at or below 3.25x after the prior holiday ends. EBITDA add-backs: interest, taxes, D&A, non-cash stock compensation, other non-cash charges (later cash payments are subtracted), debt extinguishment losses, cash restructuring/severance capped at $200m per four quarters, and uncapped extraordinary, unusual or non-recurring cash charges. There is no add-back for projected cost savings or synergies. Pro forma adjustments for Material Acquisitions/Dispositions ($75m+) are made under Regulation S-X Article 11. Guarantees come from Designated Subsidiaries (wholly-owned domestic Material Subsidiaries, excluding FSHCOs and securitization subsidiaries). There is no unrestricted subsidiary concept, no collateral and no equity cure. Negative covenants: subsidiary debt and liens share a basket of 15% of Consolidated Net Tangible Assets, plus a securitization basket of the greater of $600m and 10% of CNTA.
parsed.facility: $1.5bn unsecured revolving credit facility (including $150m LC sublimit and $15m swingline) with up to $500m accordion, maturing July 3, 2030 (two one-year extension options)

terms.summary: The agreement has no unrestricted subsidiary concept and no restriction on transferring or exclusively licensing intellectual property to non-guarantor entities.

Changes to the pro rata payment waterfall and sharing provisions in Sections 2.15(b)/(c) require each Lender's consent. However, there is no express requirement for each affected lender to consent to subordination of the loans or of any liens; the facility is unsecured.

terms.quote: A Subsidiary Guarantor shall automatically be released from its obligations under the Guarantee Agreement upon the consummation of any transaction permitted by this Agreement as a result of which such Subsidiary Guarantor ceases to be a Subsidiary;
terms.summary: Automatic release is triggered only when a guarantor stops being a Subsidiary (more than 50% owned), not merely when it stops being wholly owned. There is no express anti-Chewy language, and a sale of majority control would still release the guarantor.
The agreement has no unrestricted subsidiaries and no investment covenant, so there is no cap on designations or investments.

terms.quote: cash restructuring, severance and similar charges, including costs associated with discontinued operations or exiting businesses, in an aggregate amount not in excess of $200,000,000 in any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters
terms.summary: Cash restructuring and severance add-backs are capped at $200m per four quarters, and there is no add-back for projected cost savings or synergies. However, extraordinary, unusual or non-recurring cash charges are added back without a cap.
There is no equity cure right; a breach of Section 6.06 is an immediate Event of Default under Article VII(d).
